transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-17
Start time (UTC): 15:30
Duration: 55 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Cole (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (AeroLattice CTO), Marcus Li (AeroLattice Platform Eng), Priya Rao (AeroLattice Product)
Links shared: packaging checklist (https://redwood.ai/packaging-checklist), reference arch deck (drive/aerolattice-refarch-v1.pdf), pilot spreadsheet (drive/aerolattice-pilot-sheet)

Summary: quick sync to align marketplace listing requirements, discuss private runtime interop (VPC/KMS/ingress), and agree on pilot scope and benchmarks. Emphasis on helm packaging, KMS compatibility, and quantization tradeoffs for cost/latency.

00:00 Samira (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Samira from Redwood, and with me is Ethan, our platform SE. Quick round, could you say hi and your role?
00:25 Lena - AeroLattice (CTO): Yeah hi I'm Lena, CTO at AeroLattice, um we're running a hybrid control plane, mostly GCP and some on-prem for defense customers.
00:43 Marcus - AeroLattice (Platform Eng): Marcus here, platform engineer, I own the on-prem clusters and the CI/CD for infra.
00:50 Priya - AeroLattice (Product): Priya, product, coordinating the pilot and procurement side.
01:05 Ethan (Redwood SE): Great, thanks. Agenda: marketplace listing checklist, network/KMS compatibility, packaging (helm + operator), and then pilot perf targets.
01:18 Lena: Sounds good. Quick context: our main ask is to list Redwood in our enterprise marketplace and to validate that your private deployment can run in our air-gapped sites with our H-S-M/KMS and the sidecar envoy proxies.
01:35 Samira: Got it. Two parallel workstreams: listing readiness (billing, listing metadata, docs) and runtime interop for private deployment. We'll surface the packaging checklist for the marketplace and a tech playbook for on-prem.
01:49 Marcus: For the runtime, the big blockers we saw in earlier vendor integrations are KMS handshake timing and egress restrictions — we have strict outbound rules, and anything that tries to phone-home fails our scan.
02:08 Ethan: Understood. On KMS: Redwood supports common KMS flows, we do a KMS proxy shim that can call customer KMS over TLS. We need the endpoint and allowed ciphers. Also note our private agent can be configured to use H-S-M via PKCS#11, but that path hasn't been run in your environment yet.
02:32 Lena: Okay, that's promising. One thing — when you say "private agent" are you talking about the whole control plane or just the inference runtime?
02:40 Ethan: Good question. The private offering puts control plane configuration in your V-P-C but the inference runtime (the GPU nodes) can be host-managed or fully customer-hosted depending on the contract. For marketplace listing we usually show both options.
02:58 Samira: For the listing metadata we need the contact info, supported regions, minimum SLA, and module list. We'll send a template after this call.
03:10 Priya: On the SLA side, our procurement needs explicit language on latency targets and degradation policies.
03:20 Samira: We'll include the SLA language we use for Dedicated and note differences for Private.
03:29 Marcus: Can we talk about networking — ingress, egress and sidecar? Our infra team uses envoy as an ingress, mTLS enforced cluster-wide, and we rate limit external egress at firewall. How does Redwood handle sidecars or proxies?
03:46 Ethan: We can run without sidecars if you prefer — the runtime supports direct container networking. But we often recommend a small sidecar for trace collection and health pings. The health pings can be configured to use customer-internal endpoints only.
04:02 Lena: The thing is any periodic external ping will fail our audit, so it needs to be zero egress unless explicitly opened.
04:10 Ethan: That should be fine, we have a zero-egress mode. We do need to confirm image provenance — we can provide signed images and the SBOM.
04:22 Marcus: SBOM yes, supply chain is required. Also what's your quantization support? We've got 24GB A10Gs and need to understand cost/latency tradeoffs.
04:34 Ethan: We support FP16, int8 (quantized) and a 4-bit path for some models. Quantization affects latency and quality; we'll run a quick baseline on your sequence lengths. I'll own that bench.
04:48 Samira: We'll align on target SLOs for pilot — 95th percentile latency under X ms for typical prompts, and throughput for concurrency target.
04:56 Priya: Our success criteria: under 400ms p95 for chat prompts and less than $0.0007 per token for embedding use-case.
05:08 Ethan: Noted — we'll validate feasibility.
05:18 [05:18] Speaker 1: (mumble) need to check token calc..
05:30 Ethan: Also packaging: for marketplace we produce a helm chart and a systemd/daemonset option for on-prem. The helm chart will include values for image registry (you can pull from your internal registry), KMS config, and network policies.
05:48 Marcus: If we host images internally, can we skip any outbound auth? Our CI signs images and we pull them via private registry with a trust policy.
05:58 Samira: Yes — documentation will include registry pull examples and trust policy guidance. We'll include examples for GCR and Artifactory.
06:10 Lena: One open question is telemetry — we need audit logs forwarded to our Splunk instance; we cannot send full payloads. Is that configurable?
06:22 Ethan: Telemetry is configurable. We redact sensitive fields and can forward only metadata to Splunk or your syslog endpoint. We'll show the mapping in the runbook.
06:34 Marcus: Are there any dependencies on cloud vendor managed things for the control plane?
06:40 Ethan: For hosted Redwood, yes; for private listing we can run the control plane inside your environment. There are optional connectors (for billing metering) that call Redwood endpoints; those are optional for private.
06:55 Priya: For the marketplace listing, what legal artifacts do you need? We might need a set of compliance docs for our legal team.
07:04 Samira: We'll attach SOC2 Type II summary, encryption at rest docs, and an ISO overview. For deep security review, we'll route to our security team and schedule a dedicated session.
07:18 Lena: Great. Let's discuss quantization and model variants — we want to trade-off cost vs accuracy across three variants (full fp16, int8, int4).
07:30 Ethan: For many open models the int8 path reduces memory significantly with small perf delta, but int4 can increase hallucination in edge cases. We'll produce a small eval set over your prompts. Could you share a representative prompt set?
07:45 Priya: Yes, we'll export a sanitized prompt set and add in the success criteria annotations.
07:51 Ethan: Perfect. I'll run a quick regression on quality metrics (perplexity / task-specific success) and include latency numbers.
08:02 [08:02] Speaker 2: background noise (keyboard)
08:12 Samira: About listing packaging — we need a short partner blurb, logo assets, support contacts, and a deploy guide. We'll put the blurb in the marketplace tile and the deploy guide will live in your listing docs.
08:27 Marcus: Are there automated tests we can run as part of our CI to validate a deploy?
08:33 Ethan: Yes, we provide a small smoke test harness (kube conformance-like) that runs a few inference calls and verifies KV cashe correctness (qualifier: transcription sometimes shows "KV cashe"). We'll share the harness repo.
08:48 Lena: For on-prem GPU drivers, do you require specific CUDA and driver versions? We run a mixed fleet, some old drivers for legacy workload.
08:57 Ethan: We document minimums — typically CUDA 11.8+ and specific cuDNN builds. If you have older drivers we can provide a compatibility shim but performance may suffer. We'll include a driver compatibility matrix in the checklist.
09:14 Priya: For pilot timeline, procurement is asking if we can run a 4-week pilot starting Oct 4th. Is that realistic?
09:22 Samira: Yes, if we can sign a pilot SOW by end of Sept. We'll draft SOW and pilot milestones for your review.
09:30 Marcus: Regarding ingress latency, we need tail-latency under 200ms for some realtime features. Can you pin model variants to dedicated capacity?
09:40 Ethan: Yes — dedicated capacity gives predictable latency; we can also route critical routes to a smaller model variant to meet tail-latency. We can demonstrate routing policies in the pilot.
09:56 [09:56] Speaker 3: (inaudible)
10:10 Samira: Let's talk technical unknowns: 1) H-S-M integration with PKCS#11; 2) egress-zero mode confirmation; 3) edge image signing trust integration. Ethan, you said you'd lead #1 and #3?
10:23 Ethan: I'll lead PKCS#11 integration and run the quantization bench (see action item). Samira will handle SOW and listing metadata.
10:34 Lena: We'll hand over the network topology and H-S-M vendor contact. Marcus will coordinate.
10:43 Marcus: Noted. I can reply with the topology doc and an inventory of the clusters.
10:50 Priya: For procurement I'll need the pilot cost estimate and a short pilot statement of work with milestone payments.
10:58 Samira: We'll provide pilot pricing and a suggested payment schedule.
11:10 [11:10] Ethan: I want to call out one integration detail: if you enable the internal registry pull with image verification, you should add the runtime image GPG key to your trust store. We'll provide the key and verification steps.
11:28 Lena: Any concerns about model updates during a pilot — do you allow pinned versions?
11:34 Ethan: Yes, you can pin models. For the pilot we'll pin the exact model sha and runtime image. Rollouts can be controlled via canary policies.
11:45 Marcus: For observability, we need token-level cost reports and per-route latency. Is that part of the private console?
11:55 Samira: The private console provides token-level metrics and export hooks to your internal BI. We'll show an example dashboard in the runbook.
12:10 Priya: Ok let's go through the checklist items quickly so we can mark owners: packaging, credentials, SBOM, SOW, pilot metrics, telemetry mapping.
12:22 Samira: Packaging — Redwood. Credentials & KMS endpoints — AeroLattice. SBOM — Redwood (will attach). SOW & Pricing — Redwood. Pilot metrics — joint. Telemetry mapping — Marcus.
12:38 [12:38] Speaker 1: (phone vibration)
12:50 Lena: One more thing on compliance: we need an audit log export that includes request metadata but not payload; can Redwood's logs be redacted?
12:58 Ethan: Yes we can apply field-level redaction prior to export. We'll show sample logs.
13:10 Samira: I'll share a draft runbook and the helm values template after the call.
13:18 Marcus: When you share the helm chart, include an example values file for private registry and zero-egress mode.
13:26 Ethan: Will do.
13:34 [13:34] Speaker 2: (crosstalk)
13:45 Priya: Anything else from AeroLattice?
13:50 Lena: We want to note latency targets and that some clusters are GPU-starved; if we go dedicated we might need reserved capacity. Need pricing for reserved v dedicated.
14:05 Samira: We'll include a reserved capacity estimate and compare to on-demand pricing in the pilot pricing doc.
14:16 Ethan: Also, about model quantization: if you need a lower cost path we can run smaller open models and a reranker flow to preserve quality; that's a common cost-latency trade we can explore.
14:32 Marcus: Reranker approach might help; we should include in eval matrix.
14:40 Priya: Ok timeline recap then: Samira sends docs and SOW draft by 2026-09-20, Lena sends topology and H-S-M contact by 2026-09-21, Ethan runs quant bench and shares results by 2026-09-24. Pilot target start 2026-10-04.
14:58 Samira: Sounds good. Any blockers on compliance sign-off?
15:05 Lena: We might need a security deep-dive; can we schedule one with your security team the week after next?
15:12 Samira: Yes, we'll coordinate that. I'll cc security and propose slots.
15:20 [15:20] Speaker 4: (mute)
15:30 Ethan: Quick note — for the marketplace tile we'll need a short 75-word blurb, two screenshots, and support contact email. Priya can own the screenshots?
15:41 Priya: I can coordinate screenshots with our UX team.
15:48 Lena: We'll also need an approval workflow for the listing review.
15:54 Samira: We'll send the marketplace review checklist.
16:05 [16:05] Speaker 1: (background)
16:18 Marcus: On the helm values, do you support node selectors and tolerations for GPU scheduling?
16:26 Ethan: Yes, we expose nodeSelector, tolerations, taints handling, and device plugin config.
16:36 Priya: Ok that's helpful.
16:42 Samira: Any final questions?
16:46 Lena: Not from me. Looking forward to the runbook.
16:50 Marcus: No, thanks.
16:54 Priya: Thanks, bye.

Recap (auto):
- Owners and timeline: Redwood shares helm chart, packaging checklist, pilot SOW/pricing. AeroLattice shares topology, H-S-M contact, and sanitized prompt set. SE to produce quantization bench.
- Risks: KMS/H-S-M integration, zero-egress constraints, older GPU driver compatibility.
- Next steps: Security deep-dive scheduling; pilot SOW sign-off; bench results and helm chart delivery.

End of transcript.
